newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Pemex details natural gas 1997 trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Pemex details natural gas 1997 trade.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said on Thursday it exported 37 million cubic feet per day (cfd) in 1996 compared to 22 million cfd the previous year.
Imports fell to 84 million cfd in 1996 from 173 million cfd in 1995, Genaro Ceballos Bravo, director general of the company's natural gas subsidiary, said at an industry conference.
Mexico commonly imports and exports natural gas in trade with U.S. border states. Ceballos did not explain the drop in imports.

Pemex's natural gas unit plans to spend 1.69 billion pesos on 1997 investments, he said. Some 42 percent would be invested in plants, 35 percent in natural gas ducts, 12 percent in security and ecology and 11 percent in storage.
Of the entire investment, 1.22 billion pesos has been allocated for projects underway and 468 million pesos for 37 new works for 1997, Ceballos said.

Further investments are expected from the private sector as 67 natural gas distribution contracts worth 980 million pesos will be auctioned off in 1997. Pemex is in the process of opening up natural gas distribution, but not exploration or production, to private companies.
